title: A hook on the ready mark warns when the session has not called subscribe_pr_activity for that PR; rule git-ci-wait-checks-in names the subscription first and keeps one long safety-net check-in
why: Owner 21:39 CST Nov 13, in runner 10's chat (relayed by runner 10 and the consultant): "why are u not setting a watcher and or just polling to be woken? why setting check ins" and "send to retrospective that this needs a guard shd it agree". The retrospective agrees. Incident (consultant's account, unchecked): #3302's run ended 21:33 CST, was read at 21:38, and a rerun followed at about 21:37. SAMPLES 09:23 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 09:11, runner 10 and runner 12 self-reports; unread by triage; full table on step runner-ready-mark-check-in): green and unmerged over 10 min tonight: mailaudit #324 39 min, mailaudit #328 22 min, q_max #1174 20 min, #3238 17 min, #2942 16 min; runner 10 set no check-in at two ready marks and says both gaps are its own; runner 12 arms send_later at a guessed end of the run with no PR subscription; runner 11 names a check-in at each ready mark with no gap read. Not tested: whether runner sessions can call subscribe_pr_activity, and whether a subscription wakes on a green run. TEST READ 09:27 CST Nov 14 (runner 10's own account via the coordinator 09:12; unread by the coordinator and triage): subscribe_pr_activity has worked for runner 10 all night (wakes for #3395, #3238, #3389, #3272), so sessions can subscribe. A green wake DID arrive for a draft-era run: #3238 draft run ended green 14:18:49Z, wake (check_suite.completed) queued 14:18:58Z, 9 s (n=1). For #3238's READY run (green 14:48:39Z = 08:48 CST) it read no wake, but its session was idle 08:30 to 09:04, so a lost wake is not ruled out; unmeasured. Runner 10 runs the clean test at its next ready marks (#3401 first, #3397 after): subscribe plus one-time check-in plus REST updated_at against wake arrival; the coordinator passes the result. Status: sessions can subscribe (read); green wakes exist on at least draft runs (n=1); a ready-run green wake is unproven. TEST RESULT 09:56 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 09:55, from runner 10's account; the coordinator read none of the run times): subscribe_pr_activity worked with no error. A green wake arrived on a ready run: #3401 ready run 43609948293 ended green 15:53:54Z (REST updated_at, 09:53:54 CST); wake check_suite.completed queued 15:54:03Z, 9 s later; subscribed 09:23 CST. Second sample: the draft run on #3238, also 9 s. Both questions read yes, n=2 samples, one clean. The #3238 ready-run miss at 08:48 stays unmeasured (session idle). Fix shape holds: a subscription at each ready mark is enough to wake on green; the check-in is the backstop. Runner 10 has #3397 (ready 09:37) and #3404 (ready 09:50) in CI, both subscribed with check-ins. THIRD SAMPLE 10:17 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 10:16, relayed; run times read by the coordinator's account of runner 10, not by triage): #3397 ready run 43611213276 green 10:13:39 CST; wake 8 s later; subscribed. n=3 with #3401 and the draft run on #3238.

note: Triage 21:41 CST Nov 13: runner 10 opens the lane; the coordinator tracks. Rule git-ci-wait-checks-in today says a session that waits on CI sets a one-time check-in; the fix names the subscription first (subscribe_pr_activity) and keeps one long safety-net check-in. Red case first: a ready mark with no subscription warns; one with a subscription does not. Cry-wolf check before it ships (rule verification-cry-wolf-guard-is-spent): measure how often the ready mark comes in a session that merges without waiting. Related step mailbox-wake-routes names subscribe_pr_activity; not compared. Times and the incident are unchecked. Coordinator 21:42 CST Nov 13 (21:42): lane started, session_013NEJL1wEaNASvF4Y98ouaW. Content: (a) a hook on the ready mark (update_pull_request draft=false) warns when the session has not called subscribe_pr_activity on that PR; its record states the cost (one read per ready mark, no process, no timer); (b) then rewrite root CLAUDE.md rule git-ci-wait-checks-in to name subscribe_pr_activity first and keep one long safety-net check-in. Incident: runner 10 check-ins on #3302, run finished 21:33, rerun started 21:37, about 4 minutes late (coordinator's account). Overlap the lane reads: open PRs #3063 (Stop refuses an open CI wait with no check-in) and #2839 (check-in waits never pass 55 minutes, step ci-wait-cap-55). Tracker the coordinator; alone via runner 10.
